title: Europe 2 of 6 · Western Europe
edition: Europe countries · Six regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Europe episode two of six. First, I clear the chosen names so we can study a fresh regional group.
Today we connect France with the Benelux countries, then zoom into Monaco on the French Riviera. Monaco needs a labelled supplemental map because GeoClick omits it.

states.name: France
lines: France is the broad country south of Belgium and west of Germany and Switzerland. Spain lies across the Pyrenees; its coasts face both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.
Revolutionary France helped establish the metric system. An early definition of the metre used a fraction of the Earth’s meridian: everyday measuring linked to the size of the planet.
Use France as our western anchor between the Channel, the Atlantic, the Pyrenees and the Alps. Think of a metre ruler stretched across that broad outline.
states.transition: Let's bring France and its neighbours into a closer view.

states.name: Belgium
lines: Belgium sits above France and below the Netherlands, with Germany and Luxembourg on its eastern side. It has a short North Sea coast.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German. Its language communities help explain why a small country can have a complex political structure.
Remember Belgium in the middle of the western coastal chain: France, Belgium, Netherlands. Three languages make a useful hook for that small central link.
states.transition: Let's bring Belgium and its neighbours into a closer view.

states.name: Netherlands
lines: The Netherlands lies north of Belgium and west of Germany. Its North Sea coast and river mouths make water a constant feature of the country’s geography.
Holland is only part of the Netherlands: North Holland and South Holland are two provinces, not the name of the entire country.
Keep the Netherlands above Belgium. Remember the low coastal country by its water-shaped outline, and keep Holland as a smaller name inside the larger one.

states.name: Luxembourg
lines: Luxembourg is the small inland country between Belgium, France and Germany. Unlike Belgium and the Netherlands, it has no coastline.
Luxembourg is the world’s only remaining grand duchy. Its name also recalls a little castle, a fitting image for this small country at a three-neighbour junction.
Remember the Benelux trio: Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg. Luxembourg is the tiny inland member, below Belgium and beside France and Germany.
states.transition: Let's bring Luxembourg and its neighbours into a closer view.

states.name: Monaco
lines: Monaco is a tiny Mediterranean state on the French Riviera, surrounded on land by France. Italy is nearby to the east, but does not share its border.
Monaco’s Oceanographic Museum connects this small coastal state with marine science. Prince Albert the First’s expeditions helped create its oceanographic collections.
Think tiny state, French Riviera, big interest in the ocean. This labelled supplemental view adds Monaco because GeoClick’s Europe target list leaves it out.
states.transition: Let's locate Monaco on a labelled supplemental map, then zoom in to see its outline.
mapFacts: Monaco is a tiny Mediterranean state on the French Riviera, surrounded on land by France. Italy is nearby to the east, but does not share its border.
Monaco’s Oceanographic Museum connects this small coastal state with marine science. Prince Albert the First’s expeditions helped create its oceanographic collections.

recap: Our western chain is France, Belgium and the Netherlands, with Luxembourg tucked inland between Belgium, France and Germany. Remember the metre, three languages, Holland and the grand duchy.
Monaco is the tiny Riviera state on France’s Mediterranean edge. Its oceanographic story completes this five-place group; the labelled supplemental view keeps its real location visible.
